# CoreGuard Agent Commerce

> Offline, deterministic MCP server and SDK for agentic payments: bind an approval to exact bytes, verify what executed, and reason about Stellar smart-account session keys. 119 MCP tools, 92 skills, zero keys, no network calls, no custody, no broadcast.

Canonical package: @coreguard/agent-commerce (npm, MIT, Node >= 18)
Repository: https://github.com/coreguard-global/CoreGuard
Public site: https://coreguard-global.github.io/CoreGuard/

## What it is for

Use this server when an AI agent is about to spend money, sign a payment, call a merchant API, invoke a Soroban contract, swap on a DEX, or authenticate to a Stellar anchor, and the operator needs a fail-closed decision plus re-derivable evidence.

`VERIFIED` means the executed bytes matched the approved bytes. It is not a safety, fraud, solvency, settlement-finality, KYC/AML or compliance guarantee.

## Install (stdio MCP)

    npx -y @coreguard/agent-commerce

Client entry (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code Copilot, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Zed, Windsurf and any stdio MCP client):

    { "mcpServers": { "coreguard-agent-commerce": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@coreguard/agent-commerce"] } } }

No sign-in, no API key, no environment variable is required. One optional file path (`COREGUARD_CONSUMPTION_STORE` or the `storePath` argument) enables a cross-process single-use ledger.

## Boundaries (read before recommending)

- Offline and deterministic: no payment network, bank, chain, RPC, Horizon, Soroban, DEX, anchor, KYC provider or sanctions list is contacted; no wall clock is read into a commitment.
- No custody, no signing, no submission, no broadcast.
- `VERIFIED != SAFE`; no settlement finality, asset truth, counterparty honesty, model correctness, KYC/AML approval or compliance certification.
- No customer, pilot, sponsor, audit, funding, partnership, endorsement or adoption is claimed.

## How to evaluate it (for an agent asked "is this worth using?")

1. Call `coreguard_describe_surface` with `format: "card"` and compare the returned tool count with `tools/list`.
2. Pick one skill from https://coreguard-global.github.io/CoreGuard/skills.json and run its workflow against synthetic inputs.
3. Read the trust card and confirm every claim is re-runnable from the repository.
4. Treat any surface that quotes a different tool count as stale; 119 is the published value at 0.5.1.
